title: Mayor wants to see Stockport regeneration inspire other areas

input.lead: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead
input.summary: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead

input.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

The order makes it an offence for anyone, including the occupants, from entering the property while it is in force and restricts access only to Reports linked to the address included disorderly and intimidating behaviour, suspected drug-related activity and the order aims to provide respite to residents and protect them from disruption Closure Orders can be obtained by councils and police where a property is linked to serious nuisance, disorder or criminal activity The order will remain in place for three months initially. input.evidence_text: Oldham Council's Community Safety Service was granted a three-year Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) following repeated offences targeting retailers in Chadderton Athanial Lucas, 30, of no fixed address, appeared before Tameside Magistrates' Court on 29 July charged with three shoplifting offences at Londis in Chadderton Lucas was sentenced to eight weeks in custody, ordered to pay £513 in compensation and made subject to a Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) until 29 July 2029 The three-year CBO was secured by Oldham Council's Community Safety Service, in partnership with Greater Manchester Police. input.summary: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urgi
input.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused
